title: Detective Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to calculate a detective salary from hourly rates using 38-hour weeks, casual loading, and super. Includes National Minimum Wage, award rates, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: For a detective salary, the annual estimate is hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, with super paid on top and casual loading if applicable.

faqs.q: How is a detective salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. For casual employees, add 25% loading. Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings. For example, a $40/hour detective would have an annual base of $79,040, plus $9,484.80 super, totalling $88,524.80.
Detectives are typically covered by state police awards or the Miscellaneous Award. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides for the specific award that applies to your role and location.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to detectives?
faqs.a: No, detectives are usually covered by an award with higher minimum rates. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour (from 1 July 2026) is the floor for award/agreement-free employees only.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Detective Salary Calculations

When you're looking at a detective salary, the first step is converting an hourly rate into annual pay. Whether you're a detective constable, senior detective, or detective sergeant, the same basic formula applies: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article explains the process, including casual loading, superannuation, and how award rates affect your pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard assumption for full-time work in Australia is 38 hours per week. To estimate your annual detective salary, use:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, if your detective salary is based on $45 per hour:
- $45 × 38 = $1,710 per week
- $1,710 × 52 = $88,920 per year

If you're paid fortnightly, multiply the weekly amount by 2: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420 per fortnight.

This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more precise estimate, use [the timesheet](/) on this site to enter your base hourly rate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Many detectives work as permanent employees, but some may be engaged casually. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

If you're casual, your detective salary calculation changes:
- Base rate: $45/hour
- Casual loading: 25% → $11.25
- Casual rate: $56.25/hour
- Annual casual estimate: $56.25 × 38 × 52 = $111,150

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a permanent detective earning $88,920, super adds $10,670.40 per year. For a casual detective, super is calculated on the base rate (not including the loading), so $45/hour × 38 × 52 × 12% = $10,670.40 as well.

Remember: super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

Detectives are typically covered by an award – either a state police award or the Miscellaneous Award or a state-specific instrument. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains the minimum rates for each classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides provide easy-to-read summaries of these rates.

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees get 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, a detective salary is almost always above these minimums. Check the relevant award's pay guide to find your correct classification and rate.

For example, a detective constable may fall under a classification in the *Police Award* or similar. The Fair Work Commission's database shows the specific rates. If you're award-free, the National Minimum Wage applies.

### Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross detective salary, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $22,000 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,092 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a detective salary of $88,920, tax would be approximately $16,017 plus Medicare $1,778.40, leaving around $71,124.60 after tax. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

### Final Thoughts

Whether you're negotiating a detective salary or comparing job offers, understanding the hourly-to-annual conversion is essential. Remember to factor in casual loading if applicable, and always check the relevant award via Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides. Super is paid on top of your earnings. For the most accurate estimate, use the calculator on this site with your specific rate.
